    FAPD-AI: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit affirmed the district court's denial of qualified immunity for Officer Jonathan Zebley in a false arrest case brought by Bryant Arrey, who was arrested for driving under the influence despite blood tests showing no intoxicants.     Jack Kahriger v. HHS (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-01070 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-01070-0

    FAPD-AI: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit affirmed summary judgment for the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services in a Title VII sex discrimination and retaliation case brought by employee Jack Kahriger. Kahriger claimed he was demoted in retaliation for supporting a colleague's EEO complaint and that similarly situated male managers received more favorable treatment. The court found that Kahriger failed to establish a prima facie case of sex discrimination and that no causal connection existed between his protected activity and his demotion. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-01187 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-01187-0

    FAPD-AI: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit affirmed dismissal of a putative class action brought by Julie Thomas against the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission and TransCore LP regarding E-ZPass toll charges. Thomas claimed she was incorrectly charged $950 in penalties despite properly mounting her transponder and brought claims for breach of contract, unjust enrichment, fraud, and consumer protection violations. The court held that Thomas's non-contract claims were barred by Pennsylvania's gist-of-the-action doctrine because they rested on contractual duties. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    119 HR 1382 RH: To amend the Federal Water Pollution Control Act with respect to San Francisco Bay restoration, and for… (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr1382rh

    FAPD-AI: H.R. 1382 amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to restructure the San Francisco Bay restoration program, expanding eligible recipients and changing from grants to contracts and other funding mechanisms. Federal contributions are limited to 75 percent of project costs, with non-Federal entities required to provide at least 25 percent of funding from non-Federal sources. The bill prohibits federal funds from entities domiciled in or partnered with countries designated as foreign countries of concern. BILLS-SEL-01
